I snagged MGS 5: TPP free from a video card upgrade, and finally had a chance to start playing it. My wife can attest that I will disappear for hours at a time. Other than the fact that it's a really shit-lazy console port in terms of the PC UI (no mouse, menu-driven controls are odd for the keyboard), the game phenominal. It's an incredibly clever open world environment that has, so far, amazingly detailed things that keep me going "oh, cool" every so often. I'm only just completing the first area right now (Afghanistan), but the things that I like are:

  • You can do stealthy sneak and peek all day long, or you can run and gun, or you can mix it up and do both as much or as little as you want. Seriously, you can snipe the first three guys silently from hidden spots and then switch to an assault rifle and just go for it, or you can blow something up and bring them all running and then sneak around and steal stuff behind them and then assassinate them. Your call.
  • The Fulton system is still here from MGS 3, and is even more clever. Now, however, you can scan people and see if kidnapping them would help you or not. Scan a guy, turns out he's a Russian translator? Fulton him, and five minutes later you can understand the Russian chatter you hear people yelling or sending over the comms.
  • The R&D aspect allows you to decide what gear you want at any given moment. Want to go in with a sniper rifle, a silenced assault rifle and a tranq gun? No problem. Want to go in with a full auto assault rifle and a grenade launcher, plus three types of grenades and two pistols? Go for it. The more you bring, the more it costs your base to supply you each run.
  • Silent optional objectives allow you to flesh out the major missions and even the free-roam aspects. I was completely unaware that destroying anti-air radar guns would actually allow my chopper to have more landing zones in a given area until I was scanning a base and just happened to hit Q and ask for intel about the radar dish, and was told what the benefits would be. I'd seen a dozen of these things and had no idea until I asked.

The story is fairly linear, given that it's MGS, but how you go about executing the various layers can add depth to the game. I free roam a lot, and then tackle missions now and again. At 8 hours, I'm 3% of the way in, but that's probably not typical given how much free-roam and side-missions I take on. And I love that. I never feel like what I'm doing is wasted effort, and I almost never feel like the combat is trivial; I have to work to get myself in position to do things the way I like.

If you want something with a completely different vibe, give Cities: Skylines a try. Amazing city-builder, regularly updated, recently got its first expansion (adding nighttime). Requires quite a powerful PC, though; don't trust the minimum specs. Expect the true minimums to be a quad-core at around 2.5 GHz, and a GTX 550 Ti or Radeon 4890. Anything below that is unplayable.

As points of comparison, my laptop with an i7 at 3GHz and a GTX 740m struggles to get ~15fps, and CPU bottenecking starts at around 70k city population. My desktop with an FX 8370 and dual-GTX 660 handles it at just below 60fps, with CPU bottlenecking around 100k people.
